statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and six representative paths. No source was supplied; critique only.

paths.description: Homepage and global portal shell; represents navigation, service discovery, consent and shared chrome.
Services listing; represents category/listing templates and mobile browsing.
Income-tax service detail; represents a high-value government task and its start handoff.
Search results for “imposto de renda”; represents query, results and service-finding flow.
News listing redirect; represents editorial content and crawler-visible content.
Synthetic missing route; represents HTTP failure and recovery state.

findings.summary: The portal ignores the user’s dark-colour preference.
findings.evidence: With prefers-color-scheme: dark emulated, the probe reported color-scheme “normal” and white body/header backgrounds; the dark-condition screenshot remained the light theme.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: There is no explicit high-contrast or forced-colours adaptation.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero forced-colors or prefers-contrast rules; the prefers-contrast screenshot was visually unchanged.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations for essential controls, focus indicators and scroll affordances.

findings.summary: Route and major state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The browser exposes document.startViewTransition, but CSS inspection found no view-transition rules across the shared portal shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same- and cross-document navigation with directional View Transitions while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The login coachmark is manually positioned instead of anchored and collision-aware.
findings.evidence: Load screenshots show a custom “Para começar” coachmark fixed beneath the login button; CSS inspection found zero anchor positioning or position-try usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Anchor the coachmark to its trigger with CSS anchor positioning and fallback positions, retaining a non-supporting-browser fallback.

findings.summary: Two simultaneous load-time interruptions obscure the primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a login coachmark plus a cookie layer dimming the page; on mobile the cookie panel occupies roughly the lower 40% and blocks the service task.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the automatic login coachmark and redesign consent as a compact, non-obscuring notice with equal choices and persistent preferences.

findings.summary: Transient overlays use custom elements rather than semantic platform primitives.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found zero dialog, popover or details elements while screenshots show a modal-like cookie layer and coachmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal consent and popover with declarative light-dismiss for the coachmark/menu, with correct focus handling.

findings.summary: The services listing overflows slightly at a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The services layout primitive measured scrollWidth 364 versus clientWidth 360, a 4 px horizontal overflow; other sampled templates did not overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the overflowing fixed spacing/width and use intrinsic sizing so every shared listing component fits its viewport.

findings.summary: Shared components rely on viewport rules rather than container-level responsiveness.
findings.evidence: Computed-style and stylesheet inspection found no container-type declarations or @container rules despite cards and search components being reused across templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards, search and navigation modules, with viewport fallbacks where needed.

findings.summary: Several controls and links are below the recommended touch target size.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed target-size with seven items; the direct probe found the 28×28 menu trigger, 38×40 voice search and 42×42 carousel controls. Keyboard focus itself was visibly outlined.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least 44×44 CSS px or provide equivalent spacing without changing visual icon size.

findings.summary: The service start path is initially blocked by stacked overlays.
findings.evidence: On the Income Tax service detail, the green “Iniciar” action is clear but the cookie layer and login coachmark dim and intercept the first interaction until dismissed.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure the primary service action is operable immediately, with consent presented without covering or trapping the task.

findings.summary: The 404 state gives weak recovery and has an empty document title.
findings.evidence: The synthetic missing route showed “Desculpe…” but document.title was empty and the main area offered only an Administration contact link, not search, home or back recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a descriptive 404 title and provide prominent search, homepage and back actions while preserving the requested context.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is poor, especially LCP.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 8.31 s, LCP 21.09 s and performance 0.47; the raw CDP trace corroborated LCP 6.56 s even under a different run.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the actual LCP resource, reduce critical chains, defer nonessential code and test under representative mobile network conditions.

findings.summary: Late content causes substantial layout movement.
findings.evidence: Homepage mobile CLS was 0.212, Lighthouse CLS was 0.183, and search CLS reached 0.705; all exceed the good threshold of 0.1.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for banners, search results, consent/accessibility widgets, images and late fonts; trace the 0.53 search shift to its source.

findings.summary: The critical resource graph is large and parser-blocking.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 111 requests and 6.23 MB transferred, including 19 stylesheets and 34 scripts; DOM confirms many classic scripts have neither async nor defer and the HAR lists numerous VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Bundle and remove legacy page-wide assets, defer noncritical scripts, trim stylesheet chains and apply useful caching.

findings.summary: Legacy and duplicated libraries inflate every portal page.
findings.evidence: The shell loads both Font Awesome 5.15.4 and 6.7.1, Swiper 3.4.2 and many page-wide Plone bundles; Lighthouse also reports missing source maps for three large first-party scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory real route usage, remove duplicate icon/font stacks, code-split optional modules and modernise or eliminate legacy bundles.

findings.summary: At least one search button lacks an accessible name.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name and label-content-name-mismatch; direct inspection showed the submit and clear search buttons have no text or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon-only controls stable accessible names and ensure visible labels match their computed accessible names.

findings.summary: Touch target sizing reduces inclusive operability.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified seven insufficiently sized/spaced targets, corroborated by direct measurements down to 28×28 px. Viewport scaling itself is not disabled.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase hit areas/spacing and verify at 200% zoom and narrow reflow without overlap.

findings.summary: The page has browser-platform hygiene failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports broken/missing source maps, two Inspector Issues and a BFCache blocker; the loaded Swiper 3.4.2 stack is also notably old.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve Inspector Issues, publish valid source maps, remove BFCache blockers and review old dependencies for supported versions and known vulnerabilities.

findings.summary: Core transport defenses and cookie attributes are missing.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Two first-party cookies were not Secure and all three used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark cookies Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is essential.

findings.summary: The shared shell has a large third-party footprint.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 28 third-party requests and 1.28 MB across seven origins. No known tracker domains or exposed secrets were found, but third-party CDNs and widgets execute before user choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Self-host essential stable assets, defer optional widgets until needed/consented and document each third party’s data purpose.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The main response lacks HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, with no CSP frame-ancestors fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS and CSP frame-ancestors, then set least-privilege referrer and permissions policies; consider Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive surfaces.

findings.summary: The sitemap advertised to crawlers is not directly retrievable at its plain URL.
findings.evidence: robots.txt advertises sitemap.xml.gz, while a direct sitemap.xml request returned a 403 HTML error. Homepage canonical and indexing otherwise appear correct.
findings.suggestedFix: Ensure the advertised compressed sitemap is consistently reachable and return a clear redirect or valid sitemap at sitemap.xml if it is publicly linked.

findings.summary: Image delivery is disproportionately heavy for a portal homepage.
findings.evidence: Images transferred 3.72 MB. The image audit found 18 legacy-format images, 12 without dimensions, 10 without srcset, nine below-fold images not lazy-loaded and four oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants and responsive srcsets, lazy-load below-fold imagery, include dimensions and avoid loading hidden carousel candidates.

findings.summary: Fonts and third-party resources consume a large baseline budget.
findings.evidence: The HAR transferred 1.43 MB of fonts and 1.28 MB from third parties before interaction, including duplicate Font Awesome generations.
findings.suggestedFix: Subset/self-host fonts, remove duplicate icon families and defer optional accessibility/legacy-update widgets without reducing essential accessibility.
